articles.title: 2027 Social Security COLA: Every benefit that will increase and how much could you get?
articles.standfirst: The official increase isn't final yet, but current forecasts point to around 3.5 percent.
articles.summary: The official increase isn't final yet, but current forecasts point to around 3.5 percent.
articles.body:
Millions of Americans receiving Social Security or Supplemental Security Income could see higher monthly payments in 2027 as the annual cost of living adjustment takes effect.

AARP currently estimates the 2027 COLA at 3.5 percent, although the final figure won't be announced until October 14 after September inflation data is released.

The increase will apply across Social Security retirement, survivor and disability benefits, while SSI payments also rise through the annual COLA system.

How much could Social Security payments increase?

AARP says the average retired worker currently receives about $2,086 a month.

With a 3.5 percent COLA, that would increase by roughly $73, taking the average monthly payment to around $2,159.

Surviving spouses currently receive an average of about $1,933 per month. A 3.5 percent increase would add around $68, pushing the average payment to approximately $2,001.

SSDI recipients would also benefit.

AARP estimates that the average disabled worker receives $1,635 per month. Applying a 3.5 percent COLA would increase that by around $57, taking the average payment to roughly $1,692.

SSI payments will increase too

Supplemental Security Income is also adjusted through the same annual COLA mechanism.

The maximum federal SSI payment in 2026 is $994 per month for an individual and $1,491 for an eligible couple.

If the final 2027 COLA is 3.5 percent, those figures would rise to approximately $1,028 for an individual and around $1,543 for an eligible couple, although the official amounts won't be confirmed until the COLA is finalized.

When will the 2027 COLA be confirmed?

The Social Security Administration calculates COLA using third-quarter inflation measured by the CPI-W.

Yahoo Finance reports that the official increase is expected to be announced on October 14.

Any new COLA will begin affecting Social Security checks paid in January 2027, while SSI recipients typically receive their January payment at the end of December because January 1 is a federal holiday.

The important point is that 3.5 percent remains an estimate .

Your exact increase will depend on the final COLA and your existing benefit amount, but retirement, survivor, SSDI and SSI payments are all positioned to rise if inflation produces a positive adjustment.

articles.title: Five dead after Amazon plane crash causes major travel disruptions at Miami airport
articles.summary: Miami International Airport is facing major travel disruptions after an Amazon cargo plane overran a runway Sunday, Sept. 6, killing at least five people and sending five others to the hospital.
articles.body:
Miami International Airport is facing major travel disruptions after an Amazon cargo plane overran a runway Sunday, Sept. 6, killing at least five people and sending five others to the hospital.

Prime Air Flight 7598 crashed into multiple vehicles and burst into flames around 2 p.m., while emergency crews worked for hours to contain a fuel leak. As of Monday morning, the aircraft had not been moved, forcing the closure of two of the airport’s four runways.

The crash occurred during the busy Labor Day travel rush, with at least 55 flights cancelled and more than 100 delayed at Miami International Airport.

articles.title: Who is getting their SSDI payment tomorrow? Complete list of beneficiaries for deposit
articles.standfirst: Your birthday determines whether the next Social Security deposit is heading to your account
articles.summary: Your birthday determines whether the next Social Security deposit is heading to your account
articles.body:
The next September Social Security Disability Insurance payment is due Wednesday, with one specific group of beneficiaries first in line under the Social Security Administration ’s staggered monthly schedule.

People receiving SSDI whose birthdays fall between the 1st and 10th of any month are scheduled to receive their September payment on Wednesday, September 9.

That means the month someone was born doesn't affect this particular payment date. A beneficiary born on February 3, July 7 or November 10 would generally be included in the same group because Social Security bases the schedule on the day of the month.

The system divides most Social Security retirement and disability recipients into three groups.

Those born between the 1st and 10th are paid on the second Wednesday, birthdays from the 11th through 20th are paid on the third Wednesday, and those born from the 21st through 31st receive benefits on the fourth Wednesday.

Who should receive an SSDI payment on September 9?

Wednesday’s deposit applies to most SSDI beneficiaries who follow the regular birthday-based Social Security payment calendar and were born between the 1st and 10th.

The same scheduling system is also used for most people receiving Social Security retirement benefits.

Some beneficiaries who receive payments based on another person’s earnings record, including certain spouses and survivors, follow the birthday of the worker whose record provides the benefit rather than their own birthday.

Not every SSDI recipient will be waiting for Wednesday, however. People who began receiving Social Security before May 1997 generally follow a different timetable and are normally paid on the third of the month.

Beneficiaries who receive both Supplemental Security Income and Social Security also typically receive their SSI payment on the first of the month and their Social Security benefit on the third.

Those September payments have therefore already been scheduled earlier in the month.

Two more September payment dates still coming

Beneficiaries who aren't part of the September 9 group may have to wait another week or two.

People whose birthdays fall between the 11th and 20th are scheduled to receive their Social Security payment on Wednesday, September 16. Those born between the 21st and 31st are scheduled for Wednesday, September 23.

Benefits are generally delivered electronically through direct deposit or a Direct Express debit card, meaning recipients don't usually need to take any action for the money to arrive.

A payment may not always appear at exactly the same time for every recipient because individual banks can have different posting procedures.

The SSA advises beneficiaries who do not receive an expected payment to allow three additional mailing days before contacting Social Security.

Anyone expecting money Wednesday should therefore check whether their birthday falls between the 1st and 10th and whether they are covered by one of the exceptions to the standard schedule.

articles.title: Donald Trump, President of the United States, "My motto is: Always get even. When somebody screws you, screw them back in spades"
articles.standfirst: Years before returning to the White House, Trump explained why he believed striking back could deter future opponents
articles.summary: Years before returning to the White House, Trump explained why he believed striking back could deter future opponents
articles.body:
US President Donald Trump has never made much effort to hide how he responds when he believes he has been wronged.

Years before his political career transformed him from businessman and television personality into president of the United States, Trump laid out that philosophy in Think Big: Make It Happen in Business and Life, the book he wrote with Bill Zanker .

“My motto is: Always get even. When somebody screws you, screw them back in spades,” Trump wrote.

It's one of the more striking lines from Trump ’s business writing because it presents retaliation as something more deliberate than anger in the moment.

Trump ’s broader argument was that people are less likely to challenge someone who has established a reputation for responding aggressively when attacked. In his telling, fighting back could protect a person not only from the original adversary but from future ones as well.

Fighting back sends a message

The same theme appears elsewhere in Think Big, where Trump urged readers not to allow opponents to push them around.

“I go after people, and you know what? People do not play around with me as much as they do with others,” Trump wrote in another passage. “They know that if they do, they are in for a big fight.”

His advice wasn't simply to defend oneself. Trump also argued that the response should be memorable enough to influence people watching from the sidelines, presenting retaliation as a form of deterrence.

That philosophy fit naturally with the competitive persona Trump spent decades cultivating in business, which was aim high, push relentlessly and view disputes through the prism of winning and losing.

The words were written as advice about business and life, not as a presidential doctrine. Still, they inevitably attract greater scrutiny now that their author exercises the powers of the presidency.

A different weight from the Oval Office

Trump ’s supporters have frequently praised his instinct to fight back, viewing his unwillingness to absorb attacks quietly as evidence that he will not be intimidated by opponents.

Critics see a potential danger in precisely the same characteristic, particularly when the distinction between political disagreement, institutional conflict and personal grievance becomes important.

It also establishes how Trump chose to describe himself. His message was that retaliation could be useful, that reputation mattered and that allowing an attack to go unanswered risked inviting another one.

Nearly two decades later, the line remains notable because it requires little interpretation. It isn't an assessment from an ally or an accusation from an opponent.

It's Trump , in his own words, explaining how he believed a powerful person should respond when crossed.

articles.title: Alaska Permanent Fund Eligibility: who will be getting their payment for September 2026?
articles.standfirst: Residents waiting for the 2026 dividend should check their status
articles.summary: Residents waiting for the 2026 dividend should check their status
articles.body:
If you’re waiting on an Alaska Permanent Fund Dividend in September, the key thing to know is that this month’s payment does not represent the main 2026 PFD distribution.

The Alaska Department of Revenue has scheduled a September 10 payment for people whose 2025 or earlier dividend is still unpaid and whose application was listed as “Eligible-Not Paid” as of September 2.

So if you’re waiting specifically for the 2026 Permanent Fund Dividend , September 10 is generally not your payment date. Most 2026 recipients will need to look ahead to October, when the state begins its main annual distributions.

That distinction matters because being eligible for a 2026 PFD doesn't, by itself, mean you’ll receive money this month. Applicants can check their individual status through the state’s myPFD system to see whether their application is included in the upcoming payment run.

Who qualifies for the 2026 Alaska PFD?

Eligibility for the 2026 dividend is based mainly on your residency and circumstances during calendar year 2025. You must have been an Alaska resident throughout 2025 and, when you applied, intended to remain an Alaska resident indefinitely.

You generally cannot have claimed residency in another state or country, or received a benefit based on such a residency claim, at any point since December 31, 2024.

Time spent outside Alaska can also affect eligibility. If you were absent for more than 180 days, that absence must have fallen under one of the program’s allowable categories.

Applicants must also have been physically present in Alaska for at least 72 consecutive hours at some point during either 2024 or 2025. Certain criminal convictions and periods of incarceration can also make a person ineligible.

That includes being sentenced as a result of a felony conviction during 2025 or being incarcerated during the year because of a felony conviction. Some misdemeanor-related incarceration can also affect eligibility depending on prior convictions.

When will the main 2026 PFD payments arrive?

The first major 2026 PFD payment date is scheduled for October 1.

If you filed online, selected direct deposit and have been determined eligible for payment by September 18, your dividend is scheduled to arrive on that date.

A second major payment is scheduled for October 22. Online and paper applicants determined eligible by October 12 can receive their dividend then, either through direct deposit or by check. Paper checks are also scheduled to begin mailing from Juneau on October 22.

If your eligibility is confirmed after those deadlines, your payment will generally move into one of the following monthly distributions.

So the immediate September date to watch is September 10, but that applies only to older unpaid dividends that met the September 2 eligibility cutoff.

If you’re waiting on the 2026 PFD, the more important dates are in October, along with whatever status appears on your individual application.

articles.title: Girl Scouts’ new cookies are now for ‘man’s best friend,’ without forgetting to innovate in food
articles.standfirst: The 2027 lineup will bring dogs into the Girl Scout tradition while offering families a cookie created without the nine major food allergens
articles.summary: The 2027 lineup will bring dogs into the Girl Scout tradition while offering families a cookie created without the nine major food allergens
articles.body:
For generations, Girl Scout Cookie season has brought families together around colorful boxes, familiar flavors and a tradition that extends far beyond the cookies themselves. But children and parents living with food allergies have not always been able to participate. Meanwhile, the dog waiting hopefully beside the table could only watch. That will change in 2027.

Girl Scouts of the USA is introducing two first-of-their-kind products. Patch Pals will give dogs their own Girl Scout-inspired treat, while Girl Scout Sparkables will become the organization’s first cookie developed for families navigating certain food allergies.

Patch Pals are soft-baked, blueberry muffin-flavored dog treats developed in collaboration with BARK, a company specializing in products for dogs. Each treat will feature one of four “patch” designs representing classic Girl Scout experiences.

The treats were inspired by Girl Scouts’ “deep love for their dogs” and created to celebrate “the bond between people and their pups.” Although Patch Pals are intended for dogs, they are made with human-grade ingredients.

Girl Scout Sparkables open the tradition to more families

The second addition addresses a challenge faced by millions of Americans. Sparkables are crunchy oatmeal cookies with chocolate chips and colorful sprinkles, but what they leave out is just as important as what they contain.

The cookies were created to avoid the nine major food allergens: wheat, tree nuts, peanuts, milk, eggs, soy, fish, sesame and shellfish. They are also gluten-free, nut-free and vegan.

Girl Scouts collaborated on the recipe with Partake, a Black-owned and woman-led company specializing in allergy-friendly foods. Sparkables will be produced in a facility designed to avoid the same nine allergens, giving families dealing with common food allergies a new way to participate in Girl Scout Cookie season.

Approximately 22 million Americans were living with food allergies in 2024, according to the Asthma and Allergy Foundation of America . That represents roughly six out of every 100 people in the country.

“Inspired by Girl Scouts around the country who have advocated for expanding the cookie lineup to meet the diverse needs of their communities , Patch Pals and Girl Scout Sparkables offer new ways for more girls, families and beloved pets to participate in the Girl Scout Cookie Program while staying true to what makes the tradition special,” GSUSA said.

Patch Pals and Girl Scout Sparkables will be available exclusively online for direct shipping beginning Jan. 12, 2027, coinciding with the national launch of the 2027 Girl Scout Cookie season. Customers can register for notifications through the organization’s cookie news page or text “COOKIES” to 59618.

Familiar favorites such as Thin Mints, Samoas, Caramel deLites, Tagalongs and Peanut Butter Patties are expected to return. Exploremores, the chocolate, marshmallow and almond-flavored sandwich cookie introduced for the 2026 season, will also remain in the lineup.

Girl Scout Cookie season has always been about more than opening a box. It is about participating in a shared tradition. In 2027, that circle will become a little wider, wide enough for more children, more families and, finally, the dog sitting faithfully beside them.

articles.title: Members of the jury in the Lindsay Clancy case describe exactly what happened: “She’s not guilty...”
articles.standfirst: One juror changed everything in the Lindsay Clancy trial — the panel was ready to clear her.
articles.summary: One juror changed everything in the Lindsay Clancy trial — the panel was ready to clear her.
articles.body:
The foreperson of the jury in the controversial triple murder trial of Lindsay Clancy revealed that the panel came very close to finding her not guilty by reason of insanity , but one juror refused to support that decision, preventing a unanimous verdict.

“He admitted he had reasonable doubt after we watched the video of the interview,” one female juror told NBC 10 Boston in an interview.

Judge William Sullivan declared a mistrial last Friday after the jury sent a third note stating that they remained unable to reach a decision.

“There were three forms I had to fill out and I started filling them out, I wrote my signature on each one but then he said, ‘But I’m still not going to say she’s not guilty by reason of insanity.’”

The three women interviewed were identified as Paula , a former government contractor; Kelly , a chef in Plymouth; and Ronnie , the jury foreperson and a retired fifth-grade special education teacher.

The jurors said the member who opposed the verdict was “arrogant” for refusing to engage with the rest of the panel and for not considering their arguments regarding the evidence presented during the trial.

“He was very arrogant. He really did not take anything that anybody said,” one of the women claimed.

Another juror explained that, during the lengthy deliberations, members of the panel walked around the room out of frustration.

“Every one of us in the hours of our frustration would get up and walk the room because you just couldn’t sit anymore. And we would all go to the cart with the exhibits. He, I think, got up to the cart once very briefly and went back to his seat.”

“He would not interact with us and try to understand,” she continued. “We read to him, on numerous occasions, the definition of reasonable doubt from Judge [William] Sullivan’s instruction.”

“But he had the hardest time getting over the fact that Lindsay viciously killed her children,” she explained.

The women also felt that prosecutors did not show enough compassion toward Clancy, who was described during the trial as a mother suffering from severe insomnia, anxiety, depression, suicidal thoughts, and thoughts of harming her childre n in the months leading up to the killings.

“I just found it to be harsh — very, very harsh,” one juror said.

“The fact that they had no character witnesses in regards to Lindsay being a bad mother … I found it to be biased.”

The foreperson said all the witnesses and evidence “proved that she loved her children … so she had to have snapped.”

The jury, made up of nine women and three men , deliberated for approximately 38 hours over seven days before reaching an impasse. The members informed the judge they could not reach an agreement on Tuesday, repeated that warning on Wednesday, and finally did so again on Friday, when Sullivan declared a mistrial.

Clancy’s defense team asked the jury to find her not criminally responsible, arguing that she suffered from severe postpartum psychosis and heard a voice commanding her to strangle her three children: Cora, 5; Dawson, 3; and Callan, 8 months, on Jan. 24, 2023.

Prosecutors, however, argued that Clancy carefully planned the killings and fabricated the story about hearing a voice and experiencing a psychotic episode in order to avoid criminal responsibility.

The case sparked a major debate in the United States over maternal mental health, postpartum psychosis, and the medical care provided to new mothers.

During the trial, Reddington argued that Clancy received inadequate care from a psychiatrist and other specialists, who allegedly failed to properly diagnose her condition and prescribed her 13 powerful psychiatric medications in the four months leading up to the killings.

Clancy’s defense team asked the jury to find her not criminally responsible, arguing that she suffered from severe postpartum psychosis and heard a voice commanding her to strangle her three children: Cora, 5; Dawson, 3; and Callan, 8 months, on Jan. 24, 2023.
Prosecutors, however, argued that Clancy carefully planned the killings and fabricated the story about hearing a voice and experiencing a psychotic episode in order to avoid criminal responsibility.
The case sparked a major debate in the United States over maternal mental health, postpartum psychosis, and the medical care provided to new mothers.

During the trial, Reddington argued that Clancy received inadequate care from a psychiatrist and other specialists, who allegedly failed to properly diagnose her condition and prescribed her 13 powerful psychiatric medications in the four months leading up to the killings.

articles.title: Donald Trump, President of the United States: "My motto is: Always get even. When somebody screws you, screw them back in spades"
articles.standfirst: A line from Donald Trump’s 2007 book Think Big captures the combative philosophy that has followed him from New York real estate and television into his political career and the White House
articles.summary: A line from Donald Trump’s 2007 book Think Big captures the combative philosophy that has followed him from New York real estate and television into his political career and the White House
articles.body:
D onald Trump has spent decades cultivating an image built around confidence, confrontation and the determination to avoid being seen as the weaker side in a dispute.

Long before he became president, Trump repeatedly presented retaliation as an important part of his approach to business and personal conflicts.

One of the clearest examples appeared in his 2007 book Think Big: Make It Happen in Business and Life, where he wrote: “My motto is: Always get even. When somebody screws you, screw them back in spades.”

The quote has continued to attract attention because it neatly reflects a recurring theme in Trump's public persona: the idea that responding forcefully to an opponent can serve as both a warning and a way of maintaining leverage.

The philosophy did not begin with his political career. Trump built his public identity as a New York businessman, later expanding into television, publishing and eventually presidential politics.

He took over his father's real estate company in the early 1970s and became associated with high-profile developments, before publishing The Art of the Deal in 1987.

That book helped establish many of the themes that would later become synonymous with Trump's brand.

He portrayed deal-making as an aggressive contest in which confidence, publicity and the willingness to push hard could provide an advantage. His later books expanded on that worldview.

Trump's philosophy of fighting back

In Think Big, the statement about getting even appeared alongside other advice emphasizing the importance of responding when somebody attempts to take advantage of you.

Another passage attributed to Trump advises: “When someone crosses you, my advice is ‘Get even!’” He went on to argue that people who attack or wrong you should be confronted rather than simply ignored.

The language is striking because it goes beyond conventional business advice about negotiation. Trump presented retaliation as a way of establishing boundaries and discouraging future attacks.

That attitude became an important part of his political identity after he entered presidential politics.

Trump's political career has repeatedly been marked by public clashes with opponents, journalists, political rivals and institutions.

His supporters have often interpreted this willingness to fight as evidence that he is unwilling to back down, while critics have argued that his confrontational style can deepen political divisions.

His first presidential campaign in 2016 transformed that approach into a national political strategy.

After winning the presidency, Trump continued to communicate directly with the public through social media and other channels, frequently responding to criticism with personal attacks or challenges of his own.

The combative style has remained part of his second presidency.

The White House identifies Trump as both the 45th and 47th president of the United States, following his return to office after winning the 2024 election.

His administration describes his political career as an extension of his earlier business success and emphasizes his willingness to challenge established political conventions.

Trump's supporters have long viewed that approach as part of his appeal. Rather than presenting himself as a traditional politician, he has often described politics in competitive terms, with opponents cast as people who must be defeated rather than simply disagreed with.

That makes the old Think Big quotation particularly revealing when viewed alongside his later career.

The statement, however, should be understood in its original context. It was written years before Trump entered the White House and formed part of a broader collection of advice about business, competition and dealing with adversaries. It was not written as a statement of presidential policy.

Trump's writing career has been extensive. The White House describes him as the author of more than 14 books, with The Art of the Deal among his best-known works.

His publishing career also included titles such as The Art of the Comeback, How to Get Rich, Think Big and Think Like a Champion.

The distinction matters because Trump's business philosophy and presidential responsibilities operate in very different environments.

A real-estate negotiation can be framed as a contest between parties trying to secure the best possible outcome. Presidential decisions, by contrast, involve constitutional responsibilities, foreign relations, economic policy and the interests of millions of Americans.

Nevertheless, Trump's personal style has remained remarkably consistent across those different stages of his career.

The line “My motto is: Always get even. When somebody screws you, screw them back in spades” is therefore more than an isolated quotation from one of his books. It forms part of a broader body of writing in which Trump repeatedly described confrontation, toughness and the refusal to accept perceived mistreatment as essential elements of his approach.

Nearly two decades after Think Big was published, that philosophy remains closely associated with the public image Trump has built, first as a businessman and television personality, and ultimately as a two-time elected president of the United States.

articles.title: Engineers don't know how this 1933 Cleveland bridge is still standing despite a catastrophic flaw
articles.standfirst: This infrastructure will remain closed until further notice from the authorities
articles.summary: This infrastructure will remain closed until further notice from the authorities
articles.body:
With nearly 100 years of history , experts still wonder how it is possible that the Brookpark Road bridge has remained intact. In a new analysis, very significant deterioration has been detected, which has led the authorities to decree the immediate closure of the crossing until further notice. Now, engineers are working on possible medium-term solutions.

It should be borne in mind that this road is used by many pedestrians and vehicles every day. It is part of State Route 17 and is near Cleveland Hopkins International Airport . Among the reasons given by the Oregon Department of Transportation (ODOT), they note that it has been closed for “precaution” and to preserve “public safety”.

Brookpark Road bridge will remain closed until it is “safe” for travelers

The truth is that the bridge rehabilitation work was scheduled for 2028. However, the analyses carried out in recent months have revealed the possibility of it collapsing. They have realized that the deterioration of the beams that support the roadways is more advanced than might have been expected.

Brent Kovacs, spokesperson for Ohio Department of Transportation District 12, has provided the reasons that led the authorities to make this decision on Fox 8. “We always say that if a road or a bridge is not safe for motorists, we close it immediately , and that is truly the case,” emphasizes one of those responsible for infrastructure safety.

“We believe this is the safest measure we can take, rather than reducing the load, reducing the lanes, or doing something temporary” , Kovacs concluded. Thus, now all that remains is to analyze which alternatives are available and determine which is the best solution so that the timelines are as short as possible.
